5x_indexed_3plus2.description: Positional 5-axis: rotary axes are locked at a fixed orientation while a 3-axis cutting motion runs against the indexed face. Used to bring an angled feature into the XY working plane without simultaneous motion.

machining_surfaces.description: Surfaces or faces driven by the indexed plane

check_surfaces.description: Surfaces to avoid for collision checking

tool_orientation.description: Auto-derive from indexed face or user-specified

orient_method.description: How the locked tool axis is defined

tilt_angle_deg.description: Tilt of tool axis from machine Z

top_z.description: Top Z in indexed coordinate system

bottom_z.description: Bottom Z in indexed coordinate system

climb_mode.description: Cut direction relative to spindle rotation

finish_pass.description: Add a finishing pass at the boundary

5x_swarf.description: Side milling where the tool flank stays tangent to a ruled drive surface. Tool axis is computed from the surface ruling; produces a single pass per height, ideal for ruled walls (impeller blades, turbine vanes, conical flanks).

drive_surface.description: Ruled surface the flank rolls along

tool_axis_mode.description: How the flank-tangent axis is computed

contact_side.description: Which side of the tool contacts the wall

max_axis_change_deg_per_mm.description: Max rotary delta per linear mm — controls singularity stress

5x_morph.description: Morphs passes between two user-defined boundary curves on a drive surface. Each pass interpolates linearly (or by user weighting) from boundary A to boundary B; tool axis follows surface normal with optional lead/lag.

5x_parallel_to_curve.description: Generates parallel passes guided by a single drive curve projected onto the part surfaces. Tool axis can follow curve tangent + lead/tilt or stay normal to surface.

5x_parallel_to_surface.description: Passes follow the iso-curves of a separate drive surface projected onto the machining surfaces. Useful when geometry has a natural flow that the part itself does not expose.

parallel_drive_surface.description: Surface whose iso-curves drive the passes

5x_drive_surface.description: Tool axis is derived from a separate drive surface (not the part surface). Used when a designer-supplied axis-control surface controls inclination independently of the cutting surface (e.g., turbomachinery hub trace).

drive_surface.description: Separate surface that controls tool axis

pass_pattern.description: Pattern in drive surface UV space

5x_normal_to_surface.description: Tool axis is held normal to the machining surface at every contact point. The simplest simultaneous mode — best for shallow freeform, ball-end finishing where rake is not critical.

side_tilt_deg.description: Side tilt — reduces ball-end center cutting

5x_through_point.description: Tool axis is constrained to always point through a fixed XYZ point (e.g., focal point of a port). Ideal for machining funnel-shaped cavities and cone-symmetric features.

5x_through_curve.description: Tool axis at every contact point passes through a designer-supplied 3D guide curve. Used for fan-shaped cavities and turbine flow paths where the focal axis varies continuously.

guide_curve.description: Curve through which the tool axis passes

fan_curve_mode.description: How contact point maps to curve

5x_multiblade.description: Specialised multi-blade machining for impellers, blisks, and bladed disks. Roughs hub-shroud channels and finishes blade flanks + fillets per blade with rotational pattern about the part axis.

fillet_surfaces.description: Fillet surfaces between blade and hub

num_blades.description: Number of main blades — drives rotational pattern

5x_port.description: Specialised intake / exhaust port machining using a lollipop or barrel-end tool. Tool axis follows a port centerline curve, allowing the cutter to enter narrow openings and machine internal walls.

5x_undercut.description: Machines undercut features (T-slots, dovetails, lollipop reliefs) by tilting the tool to clear the overhanging stock and engage the undercut surface. Often paired with a lollipop or T-slot cutter.

retract_axis_clear.description: Retract along axis to clear overhang

key_concepts: 3+2 (positional) locks the rotary axes during cutting, reusing 3-axis CAM logic — cheaper, more rigid, but requires repositioning between faces.
Simultaneous 5-axis lets the rotary axes move during cutting — needed for swarf, undercut clearance, and impeller channels, but exposes the part to non-linear motion error.
Use 3+2 whenever a single tilt orientation can reach the feature with acceptable tool reach.
Switch to simultaneous only when geometry requires axis change inside a single pass (ruled walls, internal cavities, impeller flanks).
best_practices: Default to 3+2 first; promote to simultaneous only when reach or collision dictates.
Validate every 3+2 setup with collision-check using full holder geometry.
Document each indexed orientation (B/C angles) on the setup sheet for re-indexing reproducibility.

key_concepts: Normal-to-surface: simplest, used for shallow finishing — but produces zero rake at vertical wall encounter.
Lead/lag (lead_angle_deg ≠ 0): tilts axis ahead/behind contact along feed direction — protects ball center, controls chip evacuation.
Side tilt (side_tilt_deg ≠ 0): tilts axis perpendicular to feed — moves contact point off the ball center, producing positive cutting geometry.
Through-point/curve: axis pivots around an external geometric reference — used for ports and impeller channels.
Tangent-to-drive-surface (swarf): axis stays parallel to ruling — only valid on ruled surfaces.
best_practices: Add 5-15° lead for ball-end finishing on titanium, Inconel, hardened steel — eliminates ball-center zero-velocity zone.
Use side_tilt 0-10° to keep contact off the bottom of a ball-end on shallow regions.
When swapping axis modes mid-program, separate operations rather than blending — controller smoothing can mask collision risk.

key_concepts: Singularity occurs when the tool axis aligns with a rotary axis — the second rotary becomes ill-defined and any infinitesimal motion can swing 180°.
max_axis_change_deg_per_mm caps the rotary velocity in degrees per linear mm of travel — use to throttle near singularity.
Machine kinematics constraint: rotary_velocity_deg_per_sec = (axis_change_deg_per_mm) × (feed_rate_mm_min / 60). Compare to spindle/rotary servo limit.
Soft rotary travel limits (e.g. ±120° on A) cause back-rotation moves — wraps double the program length and risks cable strain.
best_practices: Cap max_axis_change_deg_per_mm at 5 deg/mm for production, 2 deg/mm for swarf/impeller.
Always verify rotary limits via PostProcessor backplot — never rely on simulation alone.
Tilt 1-3° away from singularity poles (machine pole = pure-Z tool axis on B-axis machines).

key_concepts: Swarf is only valid when the drive surface is ruled — i.e., contains a straight line at every parameter point.
Tool flank stays tangent to the ruling, removing material along its full cutting length in one pass.
Reduces cycle time vs Z-level finishing by an order of magnitude on tall walls (impeller blades, conical flanks).
Non-ruled regions cause flank-to-surface gap — verify with a CAD ruling test (Gaussian curvature ≈ 0).
best_practices: Inspect drive surface for ruled-ness before committing — even small twist invalidates swarf.
Use side_tilt ±2° to leave finish stock; follow with a single waterline finish for the wall.
Limit cutting length to 80% of flute length to avoid burnout from continuous engagement.

key_concepts: Roughing: spiral hub-to-shroud or layer-down with morph between hub and shroud envelope.
Blade finishing: morph between pressure side (PS) and suction side (SS) boundaries with normal-to-blade axis + 5° lead.
Hub finishing: separate operation, normal-to-hub axis with low side_tilt to preserve fillet definition.
Splitter blades: replicate same strategy at half-pitch offset; chain after main-blade finishing.
Symmetry: rotate the per-blade program around the part axis using num_blades — saves ~95% of programming time.
best_practices: Use tapered ball-end tools (3-5° taper) for clearance in deep narrow channels.
Hold smooth_axis_change_deg ≤ 2° to avoid surface witness marks on aero blades.
Verify blade fillet machinability before committing — large fillets may need a separate smaller-radius pass.

key_concepts: Lollipop (ball-on-stem) tools have ball radius > stem radius — used to enter narrow openings and reach internal walls.
Tool axis follows port centerline (or tangent thereto); controller computes rotary motion to keep stem inside the port mouth.
Spiral-in entry through the port mouth avoids plunge collision with the seat boundary.
Back-along-axis retract reverses through the same path used for entry — only safe linkage strategy in tight ports.
best_practices: Verify that lollipop ball clears the port mouth at every centerline tangent — failure causes catastrophic ball break.
Take light radial cuts (<10% of ball diameter) — lollipop stems are slender and chatter-prone.
Inspect first port with a probe or borescope before unattended production.
